controlled_inheritance_reproduction.scenario: Private copied executable; controlled sibling child holds inherited CLOEXEC writer before exec of the unrelated compiled source. Parent closes its writer. Copied executable deterministically returns ETXTBSY until captured sibling execs. No service or manager invocation.
controlled_inheritance_reproduction.probe_correction: The first controlled probe tried to exec the same file held writable by its inherited descriptor: child also returned ETXTBSY. Corrected probe execs the unrelated source binary to close the inherited writer.

results.scenario: spawn fence temporarily bypassed, test fixture writer held

root_cause_assessment: A concrete CLOEXEC writer-inheritance window exists between parallel executable writes/copies and child creation. Controlled probe and fence-bypass regression reproduce ETXTBSY deterministically. Unmodified default-parallel failure reproduced once; exact descriptor holder for that natural failure was not captured, so attribution to this window is an inference supported by unique fixture paths and reproduction, not a syscall observation of the failing natural run.
fix: Test-only mutual exclusion over executable copies, executable mutation/InstallBinary publication, and every fixture subprocess spawn through exec acknowledgement. No exec retry, whole-test serialization or production behavior change.
